newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity sharply higher after nuke outage.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity sharply higher after nuke outage.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures rallied sharply amid news of an unplanned outage at an Arizona nuclear power plant and forecasts of above-normal temperatures in the western U.S., trade sources said Tuesday.
"The catalyst was the trip of PV (Palo Verde) 1 overnight and warmer than normal temperatures over the next six to 10 days," one trader said.
He added that good buying interest quickly developed with some players apparently caught in a short squeeze, which was heightened by expiry of June contracts.
Short-term physical electricity prices jumped early following news that the 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde 1 nuclear unit had gone off-line Monday night for valve repairs.
Arizona Public Service said it expects to restore output from the unit by midday on Tuesday, with full power achieved around midnight Tuesday.
The June PV contract gained $3.64 per megawatt hour (MWh) to expire at $28.79 per megawatt hour (MWh), down from a high of $29.00.
But some market players said the rally might not yet have run out of steam.
"We already traded above $30.00 one time and daily cash prices are $32.00 to $38.00. That may give us some kind of support," explained one trader.
He expected a range for cash June PV of $27.50-29.50 for the next week or so.
Traders also cited strong natural gas prices as helping to support the power futures complex.
The NYMEX June Henry Hub natural gas contract closed up 7.8 cents at $2.363 per million British thermal units.
The July PV contract closed $2.88 higher at $31.22 per MWh, while August was up $2.16 at $32.47.
The June COB contract went off the board $2.08 higher at $21.45 per MWh, after trading as high as $21.85.
July COB ended $1.80 higher at $23.11, and August was $1.57 higher at $26.45.
As of 1537 EDT, NYMEX said an estimated total of 330 COB and 679 PV contracts had traded.

A total of about 7,000 megawatts of power generation remained off line in the West for either planned or unplanned maintenance. However, much of the idled generation was expected to return to service over the next several weeks.
The 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon 1 nuclear unit was expected to begin production May 29 from a scheduled refueling and maintenance outage which began April 19.
Several coal-fired plants are also expected back at the end of month, including the 750 MW Colstrip unit in Montana and 750 MW Four Corners unit in Arizona.
Forecasters expect temperatures in both the Northwest and Southwest to run one to five degrees above normal through next week.
((--Los Angeles bureau, + 1 213 955 6761))
